topic: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions

key_points: Since v2.1.224 one session can tell another itself; payload is plain text only, no history/files/context
Two tools: ListAgents finds sessions, SendMessage delivers by name — Claude does both, you describe the outcome
Requirements: v2.1.224+, macOS/Linux incl WSL2, not Bedrock/AWS/GCP/Foundry, feature-flag eval must stay on
Names are the address; /rename or --name, derived from folder otherwise; collisions disambiguated by working dir
Session registers a JSON file and binds a per-user Unix socket; discovery is filesystem-based (container vs host can't reach)
CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET env var lets hooks/scripts post into a session
-p sessions can't show approval dialog; use --settings crossSessionInbound=accept for unattended workers; bare mode binds no socket
Message = one sentence + sender name + reply address; collapses to Ctrl+O one-liner
Solves 'acting as messenger between my own sessions' — handoff of a finding / rename / schema change
Three use cases: breaking change across sessions, waiting on long migration/test, working same codebase from two terminals
No setup: tell Claude what to pass along and who to tell; Claude finds target via /list-agents and writes the note
Since v2.1.232 @-mention typeahead to name target directly in prompt
Claude also sends unprompted when it notices a change affects another session; receiving Claude can auto-reply
Cross-machine/cloud needs Remote Control + v2.1.225+ to initiate; travels via Anthropic servers; container vs host can't reach
v2.1.224+ macOS/Linux; Windows not yet supported
Shipped 2.1.224 on Aug 7 2026, finished 2.1.232 Aug 13 (@-mention); on by default, nothing to enable
Same-machine messages travel over per-session Unix socket, never Anthropic servers; cross-machine/cloud route through Anthropic
Sends a note not the conversation — use /resume to hand off full context
Safety: can't approve permissions, can't change CLAUDE.md/settings, slash commands land as plain text, per-session permissions apply
Anti-loop throttle: rate-limits repeats, drops identical repeats, caps 50 queued messages
Practical habits: /rename sessions deliberately, let sessions speak up proactively, prefer local-only default for parallel worktrees
Anthropic announced cross-session messaging in v2.1.224 for macOS/Linux
Best use cases: hand over a finding, coordinate parallel worktrees, get status from long-running work, reply across machines
User doesn't compose the message — prompt contains the intent, Claude writes it
No permission approval or config changes; /compact arrives as plain text; permissions still prompt
Verified against live SendMessage/ListAgents schemas; name is the address, no separate addressing syntax
SendMessage to accepts teammate name, 'main', any ListAgents name, or 'worker [ref]' for disambiguation
Printing output does not communicate — must call the tool (push, not pull); messages auto-deliver, no polling; enqueue at receiver's next tool round
Names keep working after an agent completes — a send resumes it from its transcript
Constraint: message never carries history/files — write brief to disk first, send a pointer; breakout uses push for notification, pull for payload
2.1.225 fixed SendMessage falsely reporting success on failed delivery
Permission laundering rule: never ask a peer to do an action denied/blocked in your own session

stats.fact: Cross-session messaging shipped in Claude Code v2.1.224 (August 7, 2026) on macOS, Linux, and WSL 2; native Windows requires v2.1.234 or later.
@-mention typeahead to name a target session directly in a prompt arrived in v2.1.232 (August 13, 2026).

Two tools power it: ListAgents discovers reachable sessions/agents; SendMessage delivers a message by name. Denying SendMessage also removes ListAgents, and messaging to subagents and agent-team teammates.
Same-machine messages travel over a per-session Unix socket (named pipe on Windows) and never pass through Anthropic servers; cross-machine and cloud messages route via Anthropic over Remote Control.
A message is plain text only — never the sender's conversation history or files. To move full context, resume the session instead.

Safety: an incoming message cannot approve a permission prompt, cannot change config/CLAUDE.md, and slash commands like /compact arrive as literal text that is never executed. The receiving session's own permission prompts still apply.

Anti-loop protection: receiving session rate-limits repeated messages per sender, drops identical repeats within a short window, and queues at most 50 accepted messages. One-shot idle notices expire after 12 hours.
Same-machine message size is capped at about one million characters; Claude Code refuses oversized messages in the sending session before they leave.

Discovery is filesystem-based: each session registers itself on disk, so two sessions can reach each other only when they share a filesystem (a container session can't reach the host session; WSL2 and native Windows can't reach each other).

Cross-machine initiating conversations requires v2.1.225+ and a target visible in the listing; cloud/other-machine sessions appear only while a session is connected to Remote Control (needs claude.ai sign-in).

angles: Stop being the messenger: the human tab-switch copy-paste loop is the core problem cross-session messaging eliminates — lead with the 'two terminals, one renamed column' scenario.
A message carries information, not authority — position the security/permission model as a feature (can't approve, can't change config, commands land as text).
Push vs pull: send the pointer, not the payload — best practice is write the brief to disk, send a short message with the pointer.
Which tool for which job: messaging vs resume vs agent teams vs agent view vs Remote Control vs channels — a decision table.
Same-machine traffic never leaves your laptop (Unix socket) — privacy angle vs cross-machine/cloud going through Anthropic.
Name collisions and why deliberate /rename matters for multi-session workflows.
Automation leverage: CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET lets hooks and shell scripts post into a session.
